name: Taer
body:
Taers are primitive, hairy humanoids who dwell in remote arctic mountains. With features halfway between humans and apes, they often draw comparisons to yeti and sasquatches.

Physical

Taers are covered in white hair, which grows shaggy across their backs and limbs, and forms a thick mane around their faces—although males sometimes grow bald on top of their heads as they age.

A taer’s skin is white, light gray, or grayishblue. It has long arms that stretch almost to the ground, and it is not unusual to see them knuckle-walking like apes. Although they walk with a shuffling gait, they can move extremely quickly when in pursuit of their prey.

Taers have beady eyes, and their wide mouths contain prominent canines. Despite this, their faces have an overall surprisingly human shape, and they are extremely expressive. Their language consists mostly of hoots, howls, and grunts, and at first glance may seem to be no more complex than animal sounds, yet it as nuanced as any human language.

Taers secrete special oils that protect them from the cold, but these same oils make them vulnerable to fire attacks. These oils also give them a distinctive odor that most creatures find unpleasant. Most taers can depress their oil glands once per day as a defensive mechanism, releasing a sudden burst of oils to surround themselves in an aura of stench that sickens all non-taers.

Social

Taers group together in small bands. They are omnivorous, mostly subsisting on fish and game. They do not eat humanoids, but will readily attack travelers or raid nearby villages for supplies when the opportunity arises.

Individual bands of taers mostly avoid each other. While they are not known to trade goods, they will sometimes exchange members of their bands to ensure genetic diversity. They will only battle each other in the direst of circumstances.

Alignment And Religion

Taer are extremely superstitious. They distrust metal and make all of their weapons and tools from stone, bone, and similar primitive materials. Their religion revolves around stone idols that each band carries with them, representing the band’s patron spirit. Most clergy are shamans, druids, or oracles, and the themes of hunting, crafting, ice, and snow are of utmost importance.

Taers are typically Neutral or Chaotic Neutral, but can be of any alignment.

Core Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are sturdy and strong, but slow to learn. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Con, –2 Int [specialized]. (1)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid with the cold subtype. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking only Taer. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Aklo, Common, Giant, and Orc. (0)
Other Traits
Bite Your large canines and powerful jaws provide you with a bite attack. This is a primary natural attack that deal 1d3 damage. (1)
Camouflage You gain a +4 species bonus on Stealth checks while within icy or snowy terrain. (1)
Cold Immunity You are immune to cold damage. (4)
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Fire Vulnerability You take half again as much damage (+50%) from any attack that deals fire damage. (–2)
Natural Armor Your tough, leathery hide provides you with a +1 natural armor bonus to AC. (2)
Slam You can use your powerful arms to make two slam attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 damage. (2)
Sprinter You gain a +10 foot species bonus to your speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions. (1)
Stench Once per day as a standard action, you can create an aura of stench around yourself with a radius of 5 feet for 1d4 rounds. Creatures within this aura or who enter the area must attempt a Fortitude saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Constitution modifier) or become sickened for 1 round. This is a poison effect. (2)
Total: 15 RP (advanced)
Alternate Traits
Climb You have a climb speed of 20 feet, and gain the +8 species bonus on Climb checks that a climb speed normally grants. This trait replaces slam.
Howl You can let out a howl as part of an Intimidate check made to demoralize an opponent within 30 feet. When you do so, you add your Constitution bonus (minimum +1) to the check. This is a sonic effect. Once you use this ability, you must wait 1d4 rounds before you can howl again in this way. This trait replaces stench.
Mountaineer You are immune to altitude sickness and do not lose your Dexterity bonus to AC when making Climb checks or Acrobatics checks to cross narrow or slippery surfaces. This trait replaces sprinter.
Snow Stride You can move through natural difficult terrain at their normal speed while within icy or snowy terrain. Magically altered terrain still affects you normally. This trait replaces camouflage.
Snow Tracker Your eyes are adjusted to exceptionally bright light, such as the sunlight that reflects off of the snow. You cannot be dazed, dazzled, or blinded by light effects of any kind—including spells such as color spray, for example. In addition, Perception and Survival are always class skills for you. This trait replaces darkvision.
Thick Hide Your natural armor bonus to AC increases by 1. This trait replaces stench.
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with the club, greatclub, and wahaika. This trait replaces bite.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1/3 to the bonus from the superstitious rage power.
Bloodrager Increase your total number of bloodrage rounds per day by +1.
Brawler Reduce the hardness of any object made from clay, stone, bone, or obsidian by 1 (minimum 0) whenever the object is struck by your unarmed strike.
Cleric Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (arcana) and Knowledge (nature) checks.
Druid Your animal companion gains cold resistance 1. Each time you select this reward, increase your companion’s cold resistance by +1. If you ever replace your companion, the new companion gains this cold resistance.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a disarm or trip attempt.
Hunter Add a +1 bonus on wild empathy checks to influence animals and magical beasts with the cold subtype.
Monk Reduce the hardness of any object made from clay, stone, bone, or obsidian by 1 (minimum 0) whenever the object is struck by your unarmed strike.
Oracle Add +1/6 to your effective oracle level for the purpose of determining the effects of one revelation.
Ranger Choose a weapon from the following list: bite, club, greatclub, javelin, longspear, spear, shortspear, slam, or wahaika. Gain a +1/2 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that type of weapon (maximum bonus +4). This bonus does not stack with those gained through Critical Focus.
Shaman Add +1 spell from the cleric, druid, or witch spell list that isn’t on the shaman spell list to the list of spells you can prepare as a shaman. This spell must have the cold descriptor, and must be at least one spell level lower than the highest-level shaman spell you can cast.
Sorcerer Add +1/2 point of cold damage to sorcerer spells that deal cold damage.
Witch Add +1 on concentration checks made when casting spells with the cold descriptor.
